children: What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after investors shifted their focus from what AI technology can do toward concerns over how companies will finance it.

Driven by these escalating AI funding fears and elevated interest rates, CNBC noted that a massive rotation out of the sector erased more than $1 trillion from the world's largest semiconductor and AI-related stocks this week.

Furthermore, CNBC explained that this funding anxiety triggered counterintuitive moves in the broader market, as investors reassessed the impact of high interest rates on corporate debt-servicing capacity and overall economic growth. Because of these rising structural risks, CNBC reported that safe-haven demand temporarily outweighed inflation fears, prompting capital to exit high-growth tech assets and flow into the Treasury market, which ironically pulled the 10-year Treasury yield down toward 5.09 percent.

Ultimately, according to CNBC analysts, this widespread tech sell-off underscores a growing realization on Wall Street that if the capital-intensive AI trade slows due to financing constraints, broader economic growth will likely decelerate as well.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming In On SentinelOne (S)

SentinelOne’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 31 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock dropped 2.5% on the news that the company announced plans to offer $1.25 billion in convertible senior notes due 2031 in a private placement. The offering consists of 0.00% convertible senior notes maturing in 2031 offered to qualified institutional buyers. Initial purchasers also hold an option to buy up to an additional $187.5 million aggregate principal amount of the notes. Convertible notes can convert into common stock, which can increase the total share count and dilute existing shareholders.

SentinelOne is up 44.8% since the beginning of the year, but at $21.21 per share, it is still trading 19.3% below its 52-week high of $26.27 from October 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of SentinelOne’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $338.54.
